cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and your eyes are steady on the work in front of you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing on your list and give it a full pass with no tools, then stop at the edge of the doing and leave it there.
cells.core:
The daily practice has built something that holds. You can sit down and watch what is actually in front of you — not because you forced it, but because repetition made it reliable, and now it does the work on its own. It shows in how you hold your instruments and how you keep going when the result isn't there yet.

The first clear seeing arrives before it cuts anything, and you are free to let it stay that way for a while. Depth can feed itself here. Let the pattern come to you by watching better instead of reaching in for it. That is what this balance is free to feed next.
cells.sheetLine: When your eyes are steady, the work goes easier.
cells.verb: letting the first clear seeing arise before it cuts anything
cells.place: on the solitary practice floor, keeping a small steady light lit by repetition

cells.tense: You are already at a future where what you see has to be certain, and you are bracing for it.
cells.ask: At the next moment you start checking whether what you saw was real, stop and say out loud what you noticed, exactly as it came. Nothing else for an hour.
cells.core:
The practice is in good shape to look at. You show up, you put in the reps, and when nothing is at stake you see what is in front of you and leave it alone. That ease is real, and it came from the repetition.

But you are running it ahead of itself. Somewhere forward there's a version where nothing misses, and every session becomes a check on whether what you saw was real. The practice turns into proving what you watched, not doing it. What gets lost is freshness — the plain, available attention that makes seeing possible in the first place. Just once, let a perception be final when it arrives, without the audit behind it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep checking whether you saw it instead of watching what's there.
cells.verb: letting the first clear seeing arise before it cuts anything

cells.tense: You stood at that first clear seeing a long time ago, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Set two small practice blocks tomorrow and keep them the same size whether they go well or not, and report one thing you saw to someone who asks.
cells.core:
There is a way this looks when it is working: you sit down, your attention lands, and what's in front of you is simply there — no strain, no reaching. The head is clear. The work is honest. That is what the practice is for.

But watching has stopped taking hold. Somewhere along the way the practice got heavy, or didn't work the way it was supposed to, and it thinned out into something you do for the purpose rather than with any real attention. What you saw at the start tends itself, but it doesn't reach your hands anymore. What's starved is the practice that would carry it. Fill the doing, not the eye. Two small sessions kept honestly will restart the current.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it, but you stopped bringing it to the work.
cells.verb: letting the first clear seeing arise before it cuts anything
cells.place: on the solitary practice floor, keeping a small steady light lit by repetition

cells.tense: Your hand is already on it, but you have not turned the page to see the writing.
cells.ask: Name one thing in your practice right now that you have been mentally crediting to luck or talent, and say that you chose it.
cells.core:
There is a way this looks when it is working: a small move in a session you actually run well, and what's in front of you shows itself before you reach for it. No strain, no story about where it came from — just the attention landing, clean.

You are already letting that through, and your description is that it came from nowhere, or that the technique did it. That description is a habit, not a fact. What enters now is not fate and not reward. It is what shows when attention is simply present, and it has been showing up long enough to be called yours. Seeing is not better when it arrives unclaimed. Saying you keep the light on doesn't make it less accurate. It just puts your hand on it.
cells.sheetLine: The seeing is already acting. You just haven't signed it.
